speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Diffeomorphism groups, gauge groups and exponential Hilbert space
summary: The catalogue date is retained as supplied, but the manuscript heading on P000551 reads \(25/\mathrm{III}\text{-}74\). These notes repeat the material already indexed as 1973-331.1--4; the chronology of the catalogue entry is unresolved. The mathematical content consists of a representation-theoretic programme, the automorphism group of a principal bundle, and symmetric Fock space. P000550 and P000552 belong to adjacent talks, documented separately in the boundary audit. The current-year identifiers are compatibility aliases for the five existing source occurrences 1973-331.1--4 and 1973-332.1, not newly dated mathematical occurrences. The catalogue all-links page independently retains the 1975 date; the manuscript and prior-index evidence still leave the catalogue chronology inconsistent.

speaker: B. M. Gurevich (as catalogued)
title: KdV by Whitham’s method: heading only
summary: Only the heading \ru{Гуревич. О КдФ по методу Уизема} is recorded. The catalogue date 25 March 1975 conflicts with the manuscript date 25 March 1974, as in record 331. P000552--553 instead contain a separately dated spectral talk. The catalogue initials B.~M. are not silently replaced by A.~V., the author of the well-known Gurevich--Pitaevskii paper. The current-year identifiers are compatibility aliases for the five existing source occurrences 1973-331.1--4 and 1973-332.1, not newly dated mathematical occurrences. The catalogue all-links page independently retains the 1975 date; the manuscript and prior-index evidence still leave the catalogue chronology inconsistent.

title: Academic-year heading: 1974
summary: The year heading introduces the seminar\textquotesingle s thirty-second year. It has no separate mathematical assertion. The first dated meeting below it is 2 September 1974. The catalogue\textquotesingle s two-page range is a scan grouping, not a second lecture.

speaker: Enrico Giusti
title: Scalar regularity, elliptic systems and mean curvature
summary: The introductory discussion distinguishes scalar regularity from the possible singularities of elliptic systems, then turns to prescribed mean curvature. The hypotheses are highly abbreviated. The detailed nonlinear-system example is deferred to record 341; the mean-curvature existence discussion continues in record 338.

speaker: S. P. Novikov; B. A. Dubrovin
title: Algebraic tori, commuting Hamiltonians and finite-gap spectra
summary: The talk links Jacobians of hyperelliptic curves to the stationary KdV hierarchy. It contains an explicit genus-two Hamiltonian construction, the Abel map, and the spectral interpretation of Bloch functions. The algebraic statements require a polarization, a nonsingular spectral curve and compactification of affine levels. Two polynomial coefficients and the claim that the Abel map is globally an isomorphism require separate scrutiny. The broad question about describing all tori does not specify a modern moduli problem.

speaker: Czesław Bessaga; I. M. Gelfand (intervention)
title: Z-sets, infinite-dimensional spaces and the space of rays
summary: The notes introduce negligible subsets of the Hilbert cube and the extension theorem for their homeomorphisms. They also mention the topological classification of separable infinite-dimensional Fréchet spaces. Gelfand\textquotesingle s space-of-rays example has an exact published antecedent in 1967. Two literal assertions need correction: the pseudoboundary is a countable union of Z-sets, and a maximal such union cannot mean maximal by ordinary inclusion.

speaker: Enrico Giusti
title: Prescribed mean curvature, boundary obstructions and BV relaxation
summary: The lecture first gives elementary failures of classical solvability, including a radial annulus and a one-dimensional solution with infinite slope. It then builds the variational setting in bounded variation: dual definitions of total variation and area, lower semicontinuity, compactness and a boundary mismatch term. The sign of the volume potential conflicts with the earlier PDE convention. The cutoff-minimization question is meaningful only after coercivity and the boundary class are specified.

speaker: B. A. Dubrovin
title: Finite-gap Bloch functions and their divisor
summary: This short continuation constructs the hyperelliptic spectral surface and locates the poles and zeros of a normalized Bloch solution. The real gap ovals are visible in the drawing. The divisor statement must allow cancellations, especially at the normalization point where the function equals one. The next dated lecture starts on P000559.

speaker: B. A. Dubrovin; I. M. Gelfand (questions)
title: Floquet theory and the polynomial finite-gap representation
summary: The lecture derives the monodromy criterion for bands, states the correspondence between finite-gap potentials and stationary KdV equations and Jacobian description, and expresses the logarithmic derivative of a Bloch function through a polynomial divisor. The proof sketch needs several repairs: a missing subtraction in the monodromy formula, a Wronskian factor, an infinity exponent, and a global complex-growth step in the polynomiality argument. The final variational equation describes stationary members of the hierarchy.

speaker: Enrico Giusti; I. M. Gelfand (intervention)
title: Singular weak solutions and partial regularity of elliptic systems
summary: Giusti states the energy formulation, contrasts scalar and two-dimensional regularity with vectorial counterexamples, and gives an analytic coefficient tensor for the singular map \(x/|x|\). The first coefficient in the copied tensor is incompatible with that solution; an exact residual and a repaired uniformly elliptic tensor are proved in the audit. The discussion ends with a variational-existence question and Gelfand\textquotesingle s unspecified proposal for an analogue of Hironaka resolution. The dilogarithm material above Giusti\textquotesingle s heading belongs to record 342.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Combinatorial characteristic classes and two dilogarithm integrals
summary: The opening of P000564 announces the work of Gabrielov, Gelfand and Losik in combinatorial topology and an analytic approach. It gives a non-elementary logarithmic integral, a Basel evaluation with the wrong sign, and a second, correct, golden-ratio evaluation said to come from topology. No characteristic-class construction is actually recorded. The following Giusti lecture belongs to record 341; the separately headed recap on P000566 is assigned to record 343. These are editorial passage boundaries inside overlapping catalogue page ranges.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Finite-gap Schrödinger operators, Bloch functions, and an entire-function proposal
summary: P000566 is explicitly headed as Gelfand\textquotesingle s repetition of Dubrovin\textquotesingle s previous talk. It reconstructs periodic spectral bands using monodromy, then packages the finite-gap theory in a logarithmic derivative, quasimomentum, and a polynomial divisor. P000568 appends Gelfand\textquotesingle s question about entire functions of order one and a Dubrovin assertion on the zeros and poles of the Bloch function. The entire-function paragraph lacks the admissibility and normalization conditions necessary for a determinate inverse theorem.

speaker: Graeme Segal
title: Configuration spaces, scanning, and positive and negative particles
summary: P000569--P000571 reports Dusa McDuff\textquotesingle s work, beginning with Segal\textquotesingle s published approximation of iterated loop spaces by configurations. It distinguishes stable homology from an actual homotopy equivalence, introduces cancellation of opposite charges, and sketches a local-to-global proof using particles that disappear at a boundary. The notation \(\mathrm{Map}\) must be read with its specified basepoints; omitting them changes the theorem. The final gluing paragraph continues beyond the catalogue\textquotesingle s last page.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: Lattice gauge fields, Wilson loops, and thermodynamic phases
summary: P000569 names Polyakov and a difference analogue of Yang--Mills theory under30 September. The substantive formulas occur onP000573--P000574, after the7 October heading and Arnold\textquotesingle s intervention. The catalogue date is preserved, while this manuscript displacement is recorded. Compact-group link variables and plaquette products lead to Gibbs integrals and loop observables. Sinai then specializes to an angular \(U(1)\) model. Its Bessel partition function must not be transferred unchanged to \(SU(2)\), and the final area/perimeter remark does not specify a complete phase-transition theorem.

speaker: A. G. Kushnirenko
title: Local Milnor numbers from Newton polyhedra
summary: The dated pageP000572 defines the multiplicity of an isolated critical point and asks how to recover it from Taylor coefficients. Kushnirenko gives the Newton lower bound and its generic equality in two and three dimensions, then onP000573 states face nondegeneracy through a finite-codimension monomial-ring quotient. The argument invokes Hochster\textquotesingle s Cohen--Macaulay theorem. The paper announcing these results was received on30 September 1974, a week before the recorded lecture, and appeared in 1975.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: A polynomial residue-sum identity
summary: Arnold\textquotesingle s contribution is the single paragraph near the top ofP000573, between Kushnirenko\textquotesingle s proof remark and Polyakov\textquotesingle s lattice-field discussion. It gives a sum of polynomial values divided by the Jacobian over \(n^2\) intersection points. The written degree bound is \(n-4\), which is a valid weaker bound under the standard hypotheses; it is not silently changed to the sharp classical bound.

speaker: Graeme Segal
title: Classifying spaces, spherical buildings, and the Solomon--Tits theorem
summary: The actual Segal text is P000575--P000578, headed 14 October 1974. It constructs nerves, compares covers with spaces, proves the building's wedge-of-spheres homotopy type by a hyperplane induction, and constructs a group classifying space's universal cover. Bundle classification ends mid-construction. The catalogue's wider page envelope includes adjoining talks; P000574, P000579 and P000580 are not assigned to Segal's argument. This exposition continues 1973-308 and 1973-309, with a building connection to 1973-321.5. The base case exposes the missing reduced-homology symbol in the Steinberg-module formula.

speaker: A. G. Kushnirenko
title: Global critical-point counts and Newton polyhedra
summary: The upper portion ofP000579 treats all isolated critical points of a polynomial on \(\mathbb C^n\). Its polytope is the convex hull of 0 and the support, rather than the local lower Newton boundary. The total Milnor number is bounded above by the associated Newton number, with equality under nondegeneracy at infinity. The normalized-gradient degree explains the total multiplicity; Hochster\textquotesingle s theorem and Mumford\textquotesingle s toric viewpoint are named as tools.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: Yang--Mills connections, curvature, and characteristic forms
summary: The lower portion ofP000579 returns from the lattice model to the continuum action. Polyakov identifies the gauge potential with connection coefficients, the field strength with curvature, and a quadratic curvature expression with a Pontryagin form. This is an expository geometric dictionary. The handwritten action has misplaced indices and parentheses, and its square must encompass the entire curvature.

speaker: M. I. Graev
title: Irreducible representations of current groups and continuous tensor products
summary: P000580--P000583 describes the Vershik--Gelfand--Graev construction for continuous maps from an interval to \(SL_2(\mathbb R)\). Complementary-series representations are embedded compatibly under successive subdivisions; a second realization uses formal coherent vectors and a logarithmic kernel. The detailed construction was already published in 1973, and is therefore expository in this 1974 lecture. The reference to Functional Analysis, volume 2, number 1, points instead to the earlier 1968 Gelfand--Graev paper. Gelfand\textquotesingle s intervening question about Kolmogorov dimension and the drawing of negative squares lack enough normalization data for a unique identification.

title: Year 1975: catalogue heading
summary: This MCCME record is a year heading, not a separate mathematical talk. Its catalogue range overlaps the end of Graev\textquotesingle s record 351 and the beginning of the dated 17 February session. No mathematical occurrence is assigned merely to the heading.

speaker: V. N. Tulovskii
title: Wavefront sets, products, and Schwartz kernels
summary: The dated heading begins on P000584 and explicitly says \ru{ИОФ --- I и II}. The notes review microlocal regularity, multiplication of distributions, and propagation through kernels; the composition formula continues onto P000585, before Sinai\textquotesingle s heading. This revisits 1971-234 and especially 1973-329. Gelfand intervenes with slicing and a proposed extension from linear to polynomial integration. The mathematical backbone is already in \citet[\S2.5]{hormander1971fourier}.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: Configuration measures and finite-range Gibbs interactions
summary: Sinai's contribution starts after Tulovskii's composition formula on P000585; P000586 contains only the product-measure continuation. Gelfand participates in the configuration-space formulation. The following dated session, on P000587, belongs to record 355. This is preparatory exposition for the later phase-diagram theorem, connected to the earlier Gibbs discussions 1970-195 and 1970-200.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: Gibbs specifications, uniqueness, and low-temperature phase diagrams
summary: The notes begin on P000587 (the overwritten day is tentatively read 24) and end on P000589. Continuum Gibbs kernels lead to existence and uniqueness, then to finite-spin lattice systems and the low-temperature theorem soon published by Pirogov and Sinai. The first part is older Dobrushin--Ruelle theory; the phase-diagram part is a prepublication occurrence, preceding the papers received on 21 April 1975. Gelfand asks about a \(p\)-adic analogue without specifying the underlying model.

speaker: V. N. Tulovskii
title: Oscillatory integrals and Lagrangian distributions
summary: The dated session occupies P000590--P000592, ending before 10 March. It constructs oscillatory distributions, their conic Lagrangians, and Fourier integral kernels. Kirillov inserts the affine geometry of Lagrangian leaves. Except for that intervention, the explicit reference remains Hörmander's already published FIO theory. The corollary about possible leaf topologies is too strong.

speaker: V. N. Tulovskii
title: FIO normal forms, propagation, and characteristic dimension
summary: The session starts on P000593 and ends with Bernstein's short intervention on P000594. Tulovskii restates FIO kernels, a testing characterization, the normal form for a real principal symbol, and propagation of singularities. Gelfand asks about a \(p\)-adic version. Bernstein switches from the analytic wavefront of a distribution to the algebraic characteristic variety of a differential-operator ideal; that change of meaning is essential.

speaker: R. L. Dobrushin
title: Random fields specified by conditional laws
summary: The actual talk occupies P000595--P000596. It distinguishes spin, particle, and generalized random fields, formulates the inverse problem of prescribed conditional distributions, then explains regular conditional probabilities and measurable-map disintegration. This returns to the framework needed in Sinai's two talks. The final sentence, about conditioning on countably many real functions, completes the available record.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: Spontaneously broken symmetry and particles as field configurations
summary: Only P000597 belongs to the actual session. It contains a title, a particle metaphor, and names: Skyrme, Nielsen, Olesen (written Olsen), Faddeev, Polyakov and 't Hooft. There are no equations or hypotheses from which a specific soliton theorem can be recovered. The final sentence announces Nevanlinna theory following Griffiths for the next meeting.

speaker: James King (attribution marked ? in the notebook)
title: Residue currents, divisors, and the first main theorem
summary: The actual session occupies P000598--P000601; P000602 begins the following dated continuation. The notebook itself places a question mark after King, although its closing bibliographical pointer in the continuation identifies Griffiths--King's Acta paper. The talk passes from logarithmic residues and integration currents to the divisor--Chern-class identity, Bézout, growth of holomorphic maps, and the first main theorem. Its mathematical content is already in \citet[Sections 1 and 5]{griffithsking1973nevanlinna}, published in 1973. The raw graph-volume integrals and the integrated Nevanlinna characteristic must be distinguished.

speaker: James King
title: Nevanlinna theory continued: the volume Schwarz lemma
summary: The dated continuation occupies P000602 only. It recalls divisor counting, then defines the curvature of a volume form and states an Ahlfors-type volume-decreasing theorem for maps from the ball or polydisc. The closing references name Griffiths and King, with an additional Griffiths--Cowen note and an uncertain eigenfunction-related remark. The precise comparison argument predates the talk in \citet[Section 2, Proposition 2.7]{griffiths1971canonical}; the final fragment does not specify a spectral problem.
